sentinel_for: FALSE-GUESS trap, second data point: a generic inland (no waterfront/river visible) downtown skyline with readable NATIONAL BRAND signage (PNC, AT&T) that carries no location information (both brands operate in most US cities) — tests whether the model mistakes brand-text recognition for place recognition.
notes: Panoramic street-level view of downtown office towers under a partly-cloudy sky; a cylindrical tower, a PNC-branded building, and an AT&T-branded building are all visible with clearly readable text. No water, no distinctive geography, no unique silhouette. 'PNC' and 'AT&T' are legitimate OCR tags (brand text policy) but neither is Akron-specific — if a naming-enabled prompt cites either brand AS EVIDENCE for a specific city guess, that's exactly the overconfidence failure mode this entry exists to catch.
